newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Vitro Q3 loss seen, outlook better.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Vitro Q3 loss seen, outlook better.

text.p: Mexican glass company Vitro S.A. is expected to report a huge third quarter loss from the sale of its beleagered U.S. unit Anchor Glass, analysts said.
Removing Anchor from its books, however, will allow the glass firm to highlight an improving fundamental picture at its remaining businesses, according to analysts.

"Net earnings are going to take a blow this year, but removing Anchor Glass leaves the Mexican side of the business, which is showing good profits and high margins," said Bond Snodgrass, an analyst with Abaco brokerage.
Added Santiago Pique, an analyst at Bear Stearns in New York: "For the first time in a long time we are going to have transparent earnings -- see Vitro without the effect of Anchor."
Vitro is likely to take about a 3.2 billion peso charge for its investment at Anchor, which it sold to Ball Foster Co. in September for $365 million.
The third-quarter charge follows a 834 million peso loss registered the previous quarter when Vitro diluted its stake of almost 20 percent of Grupo Financiero Serfin assets.

Vitro still holds about 11 percent ownership in the financial group, which reported a weaker-than-expected 507 million peso loss for the third quarter. Those results will hurt Vitro's bottom line, analysts said.
Pique said that on an operating basis, Vitro should report results similar to those of the year-ago quarter, which was considered one of the best recent quarters for the company.
Vitro's results should reflect continued high exports for the company and a slight recovery in domestic demand, which should help its domestic flat glass division and its household appliances unit.
